battlecards.why_selected: Matched or beat target pricing in Round-2 RFP and agreed to 20 % overall reduction plus tiered volume rebate while maintaining uninterrupted service and existing logistics network.
battlecards.contract_terms: Addendum effective 15-Jul-2024 through 15-Jul-2026; firm pricing for term; volume rebate tiers tied to annual spend; option to review pricing with market data at renewal.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Competitive RFP with six bidders and detailed SKU-level benchmarks showing 30 % price gaps on 357 SKUs; willingness to shift all volume to best bidder.
supplier_strengths: Broad product catalogue covering home-health SKUs
Established next-day delivery to 65 % of orders
Existing EDI integration with Choice Health
supplier_weaknesses: Pre-RFP pricing above market on key SKUs
Limited willingness to hold pricing beyond 24 months
battlecards.switching_costs: Moderate—systems already integrated; switching would require formulary changes and nurse retraining but no capital equipment.
battlecards.notes: Savings figure from Round-2 RFP analysis slide (McKesson bid $1.299 M vs $1.556 M bench, 20 % savings). Addendum signed by both parties pending final countersignature.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Offered only 10 % savings versus McKesson’s 20 %; did not meet target pricing on high-volume SKUs; service differentiation minimal.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Participation in competitive RFP forced incumbent to sharpen pricing.
supplier_weaknesses: Pricing short of target on top 100 SKUs
battlecards.switching_costs: Would require onboarding to Medline portal and data integration.
battlecards.notes: Submitted complete bid in both RFP rounds; remained viable fallback option if McKesson addendum had stalled.

battlecards.why_not_selected: Bid incomplete in Round-1 (UOM issues) and, once corrected, still lagged incumbent and Medline on total cost and rebate structure.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Presence as national competitor added pressure despite data issues.
battlecards.switching_costs: Same as other distributors—systems integration and formulary updates.
battlecards.notes: Treya awaiting corrected bid during decision window; ultimately not progressed to contracting.

battlecards.why_selected: Agreed to restructure Full Maintenance fees by mileage bucket, reducing per-vehicle cost 13-48 % and aligning charges to actual utilization without switching providers.
battlecards.contract_terms: Service Agreement Addendum (Full Maintenance) pending client signature; applies to 385 vehicles; rate grid locked for current lease terms.
battlecards.negotiation_leverage: Detailed analysis showed only 126 of 385 vehicles used maintenance monthly, revealing overcharges; potential to solicit competitive bids if pricing not improved.
supplier_strengths: Existing lease portfolio and telematics data
Ability to customize maintenance program quickly
supplier_weaknesses: Initial flat-rate structure overpriced low-mileage vehicles
battlecards.switching_costs: High—would require buyout of existing leases and re-title of fleet; disruption to field staff.
battlecards.notes: Savings validated in Enterprise analysis slide (estimated $139.9 K annual). Addendum expected Q3-2024 start.
